title: Chicken Pot Pie
subtitle: chicken and vegetables in a creamy dried-herb sauce under a flaky golden puff pastry lid
imageAlt: A baking dish of chicken pot pie with a golden puff pastry top, one spoonful scooped out, on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

breakdown: Flour, oil, dried herbs, salt, pepper

beforeYouStart.text: Thaw the puff pastry in the fridge overnight, or about 30 minutes on the counter, so it unrolls without cracking.
Oven at 200°C (400°F). Use a 2 L baking dish, such as a 20 cm (8-inch) square or a deep 23 cm pie dish.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high and cook the chicken 4–5 minutes, stirring, until white on the outside; it finishes in the oven. Move to a bowl.

steps.title: Soften the vegetables
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium, melt the butter and cook the onion, carrots and celery 6–7 minutes until softened. Add the garlic for the last 30 seconds.

steps.title: Make the sauce
steps.text: Sprinkle in the flour, dried thyme, dried sage, salt and pepper and stir 1 minute. Whisk in the broth a little at a time, then the milk, and simmer 3–4 minutes, stirring, until thick.

steps.title: Fill the dish
steps.text: Stir in the chicken with its juices and the frozen peas, and pour into a 20 cm (8-inch) square or 2 L baking dish.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Unfold the pastry and lay it over the dish; trim to leave a 1 cm overhang and press it to the rim. Cut 3 slits in the top and brush with the beaten egg.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake on a baking sheet 25–30 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and deep golden and the filling bubbles at the edges (74°C / 165°F in the centre). Rest 10 minutes before serving.

fixIt.fix: Bake until deep golden, not light; the underside of the lid needs the full time.
The sauce wasn't thick enough before baking. Simmer it until it coats a spoon heavily; it loosens with the chicken juices.
It was still cold. Let it sit a few minutes, then press the cracks together.
The dish was too small. The baking sheet underneath catches drips.

saleTip: Chicken breasts are often $8.80–9.90/kg in No Frills family packs; frozen puff pastry goes on sale around the holidays.
swap: Leftover cooked chicken or turkey: 3 cups, diced. Skip the searing and stir it in with the peas.
leftovers: Reheat portions covered in the oven so the pastry stays crisp.
doneness: Filling at 74°C (165°F) in the centre (Health Canada, poultry) and bubbling at the edges; pastry deep golden.
source: Based on tested chicken pot pie methods (Canadian Living, Tenderflake): a roux-thickened broth-and-milk filling with chicken, vegetables and peas, topped with puff pastry and baked at 200°C (400°F).
prepAhead: Make the filling up to 1 day ahead and chill it. Top with pastry just before baking and add 10 minutes to the time.
reheat: Covered with foil at 180°C (350°F) 20–25 minutes, uncovering for the last 5, until 74°C (165°F).

basic.note: Dried thyme only, and no garlic.

stepNotes.3: Basic: dried thyme, salt and pepper only.

fancy.note: A splash of cream in the filling and a Parmesan-crusted lid.

stepNotes.3: Fancy: stir in the cream once the sauce has thickened.
stepNotes.5: Fancy: sprinkle the Parmesan over the egg wash.

plating: Serve at the table from the dish.
Break through the lid with a big spoon so everyone gets pastry.
Plain buttered peas or a crisp salad on the side.

why.0-7: Cooking the flour in butter before the liquid makes a smooth, thick sauce with no raw taste.
why.1-1: Egg wash gives the pastry its glossy, deep golden top.
why.0-14: Frozen peas go in last, straight from the freezer, so they stay bright and sweet.

funFact: Pot pies date back to Roman banquets, when the crust was often just a container and wasn't eaten.

keeps.note: freeze the cooled filling; top with fresh pastry when you bake
